newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister suspended in sauna scandal.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister suspended in sauna scandal.

text.p: Russia's justice minister, caught up in a scandal over a video film showing naked sauna scenes, will be removed from office temporarily pending an inquiry, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Sunday.

Valentin Kovalyov asked President Boris Yeltsin on Saturday to suspend him while he cleared his name. His request was most unusual and came after the monthly newspaper Sovershenno Sekretno (Top Secret) published grainy snaps taken from the video. It alleged they showed him in a sauna with women.

"We will suspend him temporarily from his duties. But things have to be investigated. I would prefer not to make any decisions based just on the publication," Chernomyrdin told reporters after laying a wreath at Moscow's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
Sunday is the anniversary of Nazi Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941.

"Kovalyov denies everything," said Chernomyrdin, who recalled the 53-year-old former law professor from a foreign trip on Friday when the story broke. "He is a lawyer. He knows how to defend himself. Let him prove it is not true."
He added: "If it is true, it is very sad for all of us, just sad. Such behaviour is not becoming to a government minister, or indeed any person. We will sort it out."

Russian television stations have broadcast brief but somewhat indistinct excerpts from the black-and-white video, clearly shot using a hidden camera. Top Secret said the video was shot at a night-club sauna in September 1995. Kovalyov became justice minister in January of that year.
Kovalyov said in a statement on Saturday he had nothing to be ashamed of and would defend his good name. He hinted he would take legal action against the newspaper.

Yeltsin is in the United States at a world summit and has not reacted to the story. A government spokesman said he was aware of it but was unlikely to respond formally to Kovalyov's request until Monday.
